anyOf.description: A spec that ran. `ok` is `true`; the verdict is in `passed` / `exit_code`.

A spec that never ran: unreadable spec, desynced net/component
reference, missing board or firmware. `ok` is `false` and the run
contributes exit 2.

ArtifactId.description:
Stable index into one validated run inventory. The inner index is private;
only [`EvidenceRegistry::add_artifact`] can mint one.

ArtifactKind.description: The normalized input format. Shared by provenance producers and renderers.

ArtifactProvenance.description: One input artifact: what it was, what it gave the run, what in it was ignored, and which cross-checks it passed.

assumptions.description:
Assumptions this artifact's limitations raised, by id, so the inventory
row and the assumption registry cross-reference instead of duplicating
text.

format.description:
Exact normalized format when the parser-family token is not specific
enough. Omitted for all legacy rows whose `kind` is already exact.

ignored.description: What in it was deliberately not used.

kind.description:
Backward-compatible parser family. For the legacy Eagle XML family this
remains `eagle_board`; consumers needing the exact document form use
`format`, which distinguishes an Eagle schematic without expanding this
closed public enum before the planned first release.

path.description:
Path as the user gave it, not canonicalized: the report must read back
in the user's own vocabulary.

sha256.description:
SHA-256 of the bytes read (of the archive, for archives). Empty only
for a gerber DIRECTORY, where there is no single file to hash.

ArtifactRole.description: What role an input artifact played in the run.

oneOf.description: A board layout.
A schematic.
A netlist.
A fabrication archive (gerbers, ODB++, IPC-2581).
A firmware image.
A bill of materials.
A pick-and-place / component-position file.
An explicit assembly-variant decision (which references are fitted).
A unit-specific as-built overlay applied after model binding.
A CI spec / assertion file.
A waiver file.
A model pack or models directory.
An MCU / `SoC` descriptor.

Assumption.description: One thing the run took as true, or deliberately did not examine, without evidence for it, with the four sentences that say what, why, what it costs, and what would close it.

because.description: Why the run had to assume it, one sentence.

consequence.description: What it does to results, one sentence.

expires.description:
Waived assumptions only: the `YYYY-MM-DD` the waiver lapses. `None` for
every run-derived kind, since an expiry on a machine observation would
mean nothing.

kind.description: What kind of gap this is. Drives [`EvidenceStatus`].

remedy.description: The same path as a typed action; `other` means follow `replacement`.

replacement.description:
The replacement path: what a user does so this stops being an
assumption. Always actionable, never "n/a".

statement.description: What is being taken as true, one sentence, present tense.

term.description:
The glossary term a reader sees: the kind's, or a constructor's
narrower one (`assumed_corner`).

AssumptionId.description:
Stable identity for one assumption within a run.

Deterministic: `"{kind_slug}:{subject}"`, e.g. `"open-part:R7"`,
`"not-exercised:i2c0/U4"`, `"not-checked:drc"`,
`"waived:si/controlled_impedance/DDR_CLK"`. Re-running the same board yields
the same ids, so an acknowledgment file can name one, a diff can track one
across runs, and a renderer can cross-reference one.

The subject keeps its own case (a reference designator is `R7`, not `r7`)
and reserved bytes are percent-encoded, so distinct subjects never collapse
while the kind slug remains everything before the first `:`.

A subject the board fails to name uniquely still needs a unique id, because
two different gaps sharing one is a duplicate the registry rejects rather than
a cosmetic problem. Two shapes cover that: `open-part:unnamed~<hex>` when there
is no designator at all, encoding the typed claim that distinguishes it, and
`open-part:R7#2` for the second distinct claim on a designator the board
reuses. Both are pure functions of the input, so a re-run of the same input
mints the same bytes.

The ordinal form is the one exception to tracking a subject across BOARD
REVISIONS, and it is a limit of the input rather than of the scheme: a
designator carrying two claims does not identify either of them, so there is
nothing stable to key on. Adding or removing a claim on that designator
renumbers the rest. A designator the board uses once is unaffected and keeps
its bare `open-part:R7`.

AssumptionKind.description:
What kind of gap an [`Assumption`] records. The kind, not the wording, is
what [`EvidenceMap::derive_status`] reads, so adding a variant is a policy
decision about what undermines a conclusion.

oneOf.description: An unresolved part defaulted to an open circuit.

A model stood in for the real part: an engine fallback entry, or a
substitute MCU core.

A pin's role was inferred from the pin-rule table, not read from the
schematic.

A parameter took a documented default because the source carried no
value.

Every placed part was treated as fitted because the input carries no
BOM or populate flag.

A whole check could not run on this input class and reported
"not checked" instead of a vacuous green.

The run happened but never exercised this element: a bus device never
addressed, an ADC channel whose injections the backend dropped,
firmware that never executed.

The result was produced at reduced fidelity by a documented degraded
mechanism: heuristic bus framing, a strapless MCU model, a net held by
an ideal source.

This run MEASURED the part outside a requirement its card states: a
fact about the BOARD, not an omission of the model, so it is critical.

The producing parser has a known limitation that can fabricate or miss
findings here.

A human overrode a finding, with a reason and an expiry. The gating
machinery stays in the waiver code; this is the surfaced record.

AssumptionSource.description:
Which stage of the run raised the assumption. Mirrors the pipeline, so a
reader can tell an input-format limitation from a binder guess from a co-sim
coverage gap.

oneOf.description: An input reader (extract).
The binder, turning connectivity plus models into a circuit.
The co-sim scheduler.
The analog solver.
A check (DRC, SI, lint, ampacity, coverage).
A human, through a waiver or an override.

BootDecision.description:
The boot mode the chip reached and why. Carried in the run JSON as
`cosim.execution[].boot` and printed by the CLI.

caveats.description:
Things the reader should weigh: a strap that moved between the solved
start-up point and reset release, a level taken from an internal pull.

cite.description: The vendor document and table the decision comes from.

mode.description: The vendor's name for the mode (`System memory`, `SPI Boot`).

straps.description: Each strap pin the table reads, as the chip saw it.

summary.description: The whole finding in one sentence (see [`BootDecision::sentence`]).

user_firmware_runs.description: Whether the application firmware ran, or was allowed to.

BootOutcome.description: Where the chip's reset sequence sends it.

oneOf.description: The application in the normal flash runs.

The vendor's ROM bootloader (or download mode) runs; the user firmware
does not.

The chip jumps into SRAM; user firmware runs only if something loaded
it there.
The reset line is asserted, so the chip never starts.

The strap levels fall in a combination the vendor marks reserved, or the
card has no row for them.

CiJsonAssertion.description:
Published JSON shape for one evaluated assertion.

Kept separate from the runtime [`AssertResult`] because subject nets/refs
are internal waiver keys, while the causal evidence map is part of the
external contract. The committed schema is generated from this type via
[`CiJsonReport`]: see `crates/hauksbee-ci/tests/ci_report_schema_drift.rs`.
`why`, `waived`, `all_subjects` and `evidence` are the only fields a consumer
may find ABSENT rather than null.

all_subjects.description:
Every part and net the `label` stands for when it names too many to
print ("... and 44 more"): the whole list, parts first. ABSENT (not
empty) when the label already names them all.

detail.description: One-line detail (the measured value, the offending seed, etc).

evidence.description:
The causal evidence map for this assertion: its assumption ids,
artifacts, models, parameters and numerical error budget. ABSENT (not
null) when the run produced no map for this label.

failing_seed.description:
If it failed, the first seed index that failed (for fuzzed runs).
Always present in the JSON, `null` on a pass, unlike `why` and `waived`
which are omitted.

failing_seeds.description: Every ensemble member this assertion failed on (empty on a pass).

invalid.description:
A THIRD outcome distinct from pass/fail: the assertion could
not be honestly evaluated because its analog evaluation window overlaps
a chunk the solver failed on. When `invalid` is true, `passed` is always
false, but the run exits 3 (invalid-for-analysis) rather than 1.

kind.description:
The assertion kind, as the spec's `kind` token (`voltage`, `uart`,
`blink`, `no_faults`, `hwtrace`, ...).

label.description:
The assertion's label: its `label` in the spec, or a generated one
naming the kind and subject.

measured.description:
The assertion carried no bound, so this row is a MEASUREMENT: `passed`
is true but nothing was judged. Renderers show "measured", not PASS.

passed.description:
Did the assertion hold on every ensemble member. False on an ordinary
red, on a waived red, and on an INVALID result.

seeds_total.description: How many ensemble members were evaluated.

waived.description:
Set when an active waiver covers this failure: the reason + expiry.
ABSENT (not null) when no waiver covers this result.

why.description:
On a real red: one sentence naming the OBSERVED shortfall. ABSENT (not
null) on pass/INVALID and on kinds whose detail already carries the
diagnosis.

CiJsonError.description: The error line: a spec that could not be run at all.

error.description: Why the spec did not run, the same sentence stderr carries.

CiJsonReport.description:
The machine-readable result of one spec's run: the `--json` document, and
what the web checks panel consumes via `/api/check`.

Every field below is ALWAYS present, including `coverage`, which is `null`
rather than absent when the run was not a tolerance ensemble, except the
top-level `refusal` (exit 3 only). Inside each result, `why`, `waived`,
and `evidence` are also conditionally absent (see [`CiJsonAssertion`]),
omitted entirely rather than set to `null`.

analog_abort.description:
Did the analog co-sim trip the consecutive-failed-chunk abort. Forces
`exit_code` 3 on its own, even when no single assertion was affected.

assertions_passed.description:
Did every assertion pass or carry an active waiver. True with
`run_valid: false` means "nothing failed, but do not trust it".

assumptions.description:
The canonical typed assumption registry. Every honesty qualifier
(substitute core, coverage hole, reduced-fidelity reader) appears here
as a typed record; `substitutions` / `coverage_warnings` remain
compatibility projections of the same facts.

board.description: The board file the spec bound, as the spec wrote it.

coverage.description:
The one-line tolerance-ensemble coverage claim, worded so it cannot
over-claim. `null` when the run was not an ensemble. Always present:
nullable, not absent.

coverage_warnings.description:
Co-sim coverage holes: dropped ADC injections, never-exercised bus
peripherals. Non-empty means part of the co-sim path never ran.

dead_rail_causes.description:
Why a `dead_rails` entry is dead when the board says so (a regulator
held off by its enable pin, or a rail only a do-not-populate part would
power), as `NET: sentence`. A net absent here names a supply but not a
voltage.

dead_rails.description:
Nets that name themselves a supply but that nothing powered, and the
output rails of regulators the board holds off. Non-empty means every
result below was solved with these rails at 0 V.

elapsed_s.description: Wall-clock duration of the run, in seconds.

evidence.description:
One causal evidence map per evaluated assertion, board-scoped maps
included. Each map's `assumptions` ids resolve in `assumptions` above.

exit_code.description:
The process exit code this run contributes: 0 green, 1 red, 3 invalid
for analysis. Never 2 here, a spec error is the error variant instead.

glossary.description:
Plain-English explanations of the terms this report uses (its verdict
and each assumption's `term`), from `hauksbee_ir::glossary`, so every
surface explains them in the same words.

inventory.description:
Exact files this run consumed (board, firmware, spec, models), with
content hashes: the input inventory the evidence maps refer to.

ok.description:
Always `true` on a report line. A `false` here is the error variant,
which carries `error` and none of the fields below.

passed.description:
The OVERALL verdict: `exit_code == 0`. Green only when the run was
trustworthy AND every assertion held. Never read this without
`run_valid`: `assertions_passed` alone can be true over a run whose
analog side collapsed.

results.description:
One entry per assertion, in spec order. An `hwtrace` assertion expands
to one entry per (channel, feature), so this can be longer than the
spec's `[[assert]]` list.

run_valid.description:
Was the run trustworthy: `false` when the analog co-sim aborted or any
assertion's evaluation window overlapped a failed solve chunk.

seeds.description: How many ensemble members ran (fuzz seeds, or tolerance members).

spec_name.description: The spec's `name`, or its file stem when the spec did not set one.

substitutions.description:
One entry per MCU co-simulated on a SUBSTITUTE core. Non-empty means a
green verdict does not vouch for firmware on the requested silicon.

timing_coverage.description: Measured timing coverage per live MCU backend.

timing_refusals.description: Explicit reasons timing evidence was invalidated.

verdict_conditions.description:
The assumptions a pass rests on beyond its assertions, one sentence
each: open variant or corner sets the member sweep could not cross in
full (see `verdict_conditions` in the engine run report), and each
passing assertion's time bound a host-paced MCU clock left unjudged. A
pass with any is conditional, never clean. Additive; omitted when empty.

waiver_notes.description:
Waiver-file housekeeping: a lapsed waiver, an active waiver that matched
nothing, a malformed file that was ignored.

Contribution.description: One concrete thing an artifact contributed to the run.

detail.description:
The specifics, one sentence, e.g. "netlist read from the document's
`LogicalNet` section, not reverse-engineered from copper".

CrossCheck.description:
A cross-check the reader ran between two sources, and whether they agreed.

The sources sit inside (or across) artifacts. A disagreement additionally
raises a parser-limitation assumption; an agreement is positive evidence and
belongs in the inventory in its own right.

EntityKind.description:
What results the assumption taints.

Scope is the input to the on-path decision: the causal-path traversal
compares an assertion's subject nets and refs against these, and only
assumptions that match land in an [`EvidenceMap`].

oneOf.description: A placed component or footprint.
One pin on a placed component.
A logical bus or peripheral.
An input artifact.
A board-level object that is not one of the narrower kinds.

ErrorBudget.description: How good a number is: integration tolerances, which method produced which time window, the accepted residual, the windows with no valid solution, and model uncertainty.

event_time_error_s.description:
Worst-case timestamp error for events, seconds. Today this is the
co-sim chunk quantization: an edge is observed at a chunk boundary.
Constructed only from a finite, non-negative value.

failed_windows.description:
Windows with NO valid solution: the run held stale values there. Any
quantity read inside one of these is not a measurement.

methods.description: Which method produced which span. One entry for a homogeneous run.

model_uncertainty.description: Interval bounds models place on parameters behind these numbers.

residual.description:
The accepted Newton residual, when the producing path measured one.
Present only when the producer measured a finite, non-negative residual.

tolerance.description: The solver settings the numbers were produced under.

artifacts.description: Indices into the run's `inventory`, causal only.

assertion.description: The assertion or finding this map belongs to.

assumptions.description: On-path assumptions, by id into the run's assumption registry.

coverage.description: Statistical coverage wording for ensemble assertions.

error_budget.description: How good the numbers behind this assertion are.

model_groups.description:
The same models grouped by their shared model, source and confidence,
used instead of `models` when the list is long.

models.description: Models bound on the causal path, one row each.

parameter_groups.description:
The same parameters grouped by their shared value and origin, used
instead of `parameters` when the list is long.

parameters.description: Parameters read on the causal path, one row each.

status.description:
How much this conclusion is entitled to claim, derived from the
assumptions on its causal path.

EvidenceStatus.description:
How much a conclusion is entitled to claim, derived from the assumptions on
its causal path. Ordered by severity: `Clean < Qualified < Undermined`.

Use [`EvidenceStatus::as_str`] on every surface. One of the surfaces this
feeds is hand-serialized JSON rather than serde output, and a module whose
purpose is that surfaces cannot drift should not have five call sites
spelling `"undermined"` themselves.

oneOf.description: No on-path assumptions. The conclusion stands on evidence alone.

On-path assumptions exist but none is critical: the conclusion holds
with named caveats.

A critical assumption sits on the causal path. The conclusion is not
entitled to a verdict: invalid for analysis, exit-code-3 semantics.

ExecutionEvidence.description: Evidence that the firmware executed on one MCU during the run.

blockers.description: Why the run is not eligible, one sentence per reason; empty when it is.

boot.description:
The boot mode the board's straps selected and why, for a chip whose
card carries a boot table (hauksbee-ir's vocabulary).

clock_source.description: Where the core's clock comes from, in words.

clock_valid.description: Whether the board supplies the clock the core runs from.

executed.description:
Any positive evidence the firmware ran: entry reached, UART bytes, or a
GPIO toggle.

faults.description: Fault or exception handlers entered, or a crashed core.

firmware_pass_eligible.description:
Executed, no fault, not held in reset, supply not invalid and clock not
broken. Only an eligible MCU's firmware behaviour can count as a pass.

gpio_toggles.description: Output edges per GPIO pin (`"PA5"`), firmware-driven.

instructions.description: Instructions retired (cycles on simavr), when the backend counts them.

pc_samples.description:
Program-counter samples taken at chunk boundaries, and how many
distinct values they held (one distinct value: a parked core).

reached_entry.description: Whether the core reached the firmware's entry symbol (`main`).

reset_held.description: Whether the board held the reset line asserted for the whole run.

supply_v.description: Lowest supply-pad voltage at the end of the run.

supply_valid.description: Whether the supply pads sat inside the part's operating range.

IgnoredInput.description: One member or section of an artifact that was deliberately not used.

what.description:
The member: a file inside an archive, a section of a document, or a
sibling file the reader saw and skipped.

IntegrationMethod.description: The integration algorithm used for a solved window.

oneOf.description: Trapezoidal integration.
Second-order Gear integration.
Backward Euler integration.
Backward Euler after reducing the step.
Backward Euler after rebuilding the local state.
Backward Euler over recursively subdivided chunks.

IntegrationTolerance.description: The solver's convergence and truncation-error settings for this result.

chgtol.description: Charge tolerance, coulombs (capacitor local truncation error).

reltol.description:
Relative tolerance for Newton convergence and local-truncation-error
control.

MatchConfidence.description: Confidence in a model or parameter match.

ModelGroup.description: The models of one evidence map that share a model, source and confidence.

layer.description: Storage layer of the model's source.

references.description: The parts bound to it, in the order the map lists them.

source.description: The canonical source, validation and uncertainty record, stated once.

subjects.description:
Causal identity of each part, parallel to `references`. Absent when
every identity is its reference.

ModelIntervalKind.description:
Interval bounds a model places on a derived quantity.

This is the socket for interval models: shaped before its producer exists so
that work lands in this vocabulary instead of inventing a second one.

Both bounds are real numbers. A one-sided datasheet limit ("at least 100")
is [`ModelUncertainty::Unknown`] until a defensible other bound exists. A
producer must never turn a typical value or an invented physical cap into a
guaranteed two-sided accuracy interval.

oneOf.description: Published finite minimum and maximum specification limits.
Finite error bounds established by empirical validation.
A published typical spread; informative, but not guaranteed.
A finite engineering estimate; informative, but not validated.

ModelLayer.description: One layer of the model-resolution ladder.

oneOf.description: The producer recorded a resolved model but not which ladder layer won.

ModelOnPath.description: A model on the causal path.

reference.description: The part it is bound to.

source.description: The canonical source, validation and uncertainty record.

subject.description: Injective causal identity of the exact component occurrence.

ModelSource.description:
Canonical provenance and accuracy record for one selected model. Every
report surface carries this object verbatim.

ModelSourceTier.description:
Semantic rung in the model-source policy.

This is deliberately distinct from [`ModelLayer`]: a layer says where bytes
were loaded from, while a tier says how authoritative the model is. An explicit user model remains the
override escape hatch; otherwise vendor SPICE and curated sources outrank an
extracted draft, which outranks a deliberately estimated fallback.

oneOf.description: A measured or source-published finite interval.

No defensible numeric interval is available. Unknown is data, never an
omitted field and never a made-up percentage.

ModelValidation.description:
What validation the selected model has actually passed. These names say
nothing about unmeasured accuracy: range checking is not curve validation.

NetScope.description: The net and optional observation interval an assertion causally reads.

Observed.description: A fact the run either observed, observed false, or could not observe.

OverrideSource.description: How a user-authored override entered the run.

ParameterGroup.description: The parameters of one evidence map that share a value and origin.

parameters.description:
Reference-qualified parameter names ("R7.resistance"), in the order the
map lists them.

subjects.description:
Causal identity of each parameter's component, parallel to
`parameters`. Absent when the parameters in the group have none; a
group never mixes parameters with and without one.

value.description: Rendered value shared by every parameter in the group.

ParameterProvenance.description: Provenance for one bound parameter of one device.

parameter.description:
Reference-qualified, so an evidence map can select by part:
"R7.resistance", "U1.model", "Q2.beta".

subject.description:
Injective causal identity of the component occurrence, when the
producer has one. Kept separate from human-readable `parameter` so a
literal reference cannot collide with generated display prose.

ParameterRef.description: One model or input parameter on a specific causal subject.

Refusal.description:
The C5.3 refusal contract.

Exit 3 means the requested claim could not be made; it is neither a finding
nor a malformed-input error.  Every renderer carries these same four answers
so a refusal is actionable and does not discard work that remains valid.

claim.description: The conclusion the run declined to make.

missing_prerequisite.description: The concrete absent or invalid prerequisite that blocked that claim.

next_action.description: The cheapest concrete action that can make the claim answerable.

valid_partial_conclusions.description: Conclusions/artifacts produced by the run that remain trustworthy.

Remedy.description:
What a reader does to close an assumption, as data.

The web app turns it into a button, the CLI into a command
([`Remedy::cli_hint`]). The prose
[`Assumption::replacement`] stays the fallback, and `Other` means "follow
the prose".

oneOf.description:
Declare a supply on `net` in the spec. `volts_hint` is the least the
part behind it needs, when known.
Write or draft a model for the part.
Put the manufacturer part number on the part.
Mark the part not fitted.

Two different parts share `reference`; rename one in the design.
`conflict` says how they differ.
Give the spec firmware to run.

Supply a BOM beside the board: it marks the parts that are not fitted
and supplies the values a board file does not carry.
Install a simulator backend (`hauksbee install <id>`).
Put the project's rules file (e.g. `.kicad_pro`) beside the board.
No typed action: follow the assumption's `replacement` sentence.

Residual.description: The final accepted Newton residual, worst node.

at.description: The node or branch carrying it, for the "who" question.

max_abs.description: `max |f(x)|` over node KCL rows at acceptance, amperes.

oneOf.description:
The whole run, e.g. every placed part treated as fitted because there
was no BOM at all.
Specific typed subjects.
One subject-qualified parameter.
Specific nets, optionally restricted to an observation window.
One named check ("drc", "si", "lint"), for `NotChecked` and `Waived`.

kind.description: The specific rule inside the check, when the scope is that narrow.

StrapReading.description: One strap pin as the chip saw it at reset release.

basis.description:
Why the pin reads that level when the voltage alone does not say: an
internal pull on an undriven pad, or the net left unconnected.

net.description: The board net on the pin, when it has one.

pin.description: The pin's name for a reader (`BOOT0`, `GPIO0`).

role.description: The pin role in the model card (`boot0`, `gpio0`).

volts.description: The solved voltage on the pin, when the board defines one.

StrapReadingLevel.description: The level a strap pin was read at.

oneOf.description: Between the chip's low and high thresholds, or no voltage was solved.

Term.description:
A term a report can show a reader.

The wire name (`snake_case`) is what report JSON and the web app key on.
Declaration order is display order; `Term::iter()` lists every term (for a
full glossary endpoint).

oneOf.description: A pass that holds only under the listed assumptions ("qualified").

TermEntry.description: One glossary row: a term's display label, what it means, and what to do.

label.description: How the term is displayed, e.g. `Open part`.

short.description: What it means, in one or two plain sentences.

what_to_do.description: What the reader does about it.

TimeWindow.description: A sim-time window, seconds, half-open `[start_s, end_s)`.

TimingCoverage.description:
Measured timing capability of one live MCU backend, or of the digital
logic evaluated once per chunk, at the configured chunk.

chunk_s.description: Actual solver/MCU slice selected for the run.

cycle_exact.description: Push callbacks carry exact cycles; poll backends carry slice boundaries.

mcu_ref.description: The MCU reference, or the comma-joined chunk-sampled logic references.

minimum_guaranteed_pulse_s.description:
Pulse width guaranteed to include an observable event. Push callbacks
see a one-cycle pulse. Polling uses two slices so at least one poll lies
strictly inside the pulse even when an edge coincides with a boundary.

timestamp_precision_s.description: Worst-case timestamp uncertainty: one MCU cycle or one poll chunk.

ValueOrigin.description: Where a bound parameter's value came from.

oneOf.description: Read from an input artifact, by index into the run inventory.

field.description: Which field of the artifact carried it.

oneOf.description:
From a resolved model. `layer` is the model source layer ("builtin",
"pack", "user-dir", "user-config-dir", "models-dir", "spice",
"engine-fallback"); `confidence` is the match confidence's display form
("exact" through "guessed").

layer.description: Which layer of the model ladder it came from.

oneOf.description: A documented default, naming the assumption that records it.
The user overrode it (an as-built overlay, a spec field, a CLI flag).

WindowMethod.description:
One window and the integration method that produced it.

The primary method covers most runs in a single entry; a per-chunk fallback
ladder contributes one entry per fallback-solved window, using that
machinery's own stable method names verbatim ("trapezoidal", "gear2",
"backward-euler", "reduced-step", "cold-start-backward-euler",
"subdivided-backward-euler").

A multi-spec invocation prints one line per spec (NDJSON) and may mix the two. schema_version 2. GENERATED from `CiJsonLine` and `CiJsonAssertion` in crates/hauksbee-ci/src/report.rs.
